messages:
maya: quick question about service account scoping in the SDK — we have customers that want per-project isolation but a single service account. what's the idiomatic pattern for mapping requests to org/project?

jared: short answer: avoid baking project into a long-lived SA key. use short-lived tokens (OIDC/JWT exchange) with a project claim or audience so the server can enforce scope.

sam: adding: for server-to-server flows we recommend workload identity / OIDC provider -> token exchange. the exchanged token should have 'aud' set to the redwood token-exchange endpoint or to the specific project resource.

maya: example token claim people use? do we expect custom claim name?

jared: common approach: issuer = customer-idp, sub = service-account@customer, and a custom claim like "redwood_project": "proj_123" or scopes array ["redwood:project:proj_123"]. our backend checks that claim and ties metrics/billing to that project. avoid relying on sub alone.

lee: note on SDK behavior: cache token per (service-account, project) tuple. if you cache globally you'll leak cross-project requests. also refresh proactively before expiry (eg refresh at 80% lifetime).

maya: sounds good. any guidance for handling 401s from short-lived tokens? retries?

sam: yes — on 401 do a single in-flight refresh and retry the request once. don't flood the token endpoint with parallel refreshes. implement a lock or singleflight.

jared: and for streaming (server push / chunked responses): tokens expire mid-stream. best practice is to: 1) keep streams short-lived OR 2) if you must long-poll, re-open the stream after refresh. there is no safe resume for delta streaming since KV cache/sequence may not align.

maya: oh interesting — so we shouldn't try to silently refresh and continue a gRPC stream?

jared: right. gRPC: metadata is sent on stream start. you must recreate a new stream with fresh metadata. for node/python SDKs we surface a callback/hook: onAuthRefresh -> app can decide to recreate stream.

lee: SDK-level implementation detail: for streaming clients we expose a TokenProvider interface. the streaming wrapper calls provider.getToken() at connect time. getToken() should be cheap (cached) and refresh transparently. we also provide an onTokenExpiry callback so apps can react and reconnect gracefully.

maya: what about retries/backoff for 429/5xx vs auth errors?

sam: treat 401 specially (trigger refresh+single retry). For 429/5xx use exponential backoff with jitter. For idempotent endpoints you can retry automatically; for non-idempotent (writes) require caller opt-in.

jared: small code snippet (python) for refresh logic we use internally:

```python
# naive sketch
class TokenCache:
    def __init__(self):
        self._token = None
        self._expiry = 0
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def get(self):
        now = time.time()
        if self._token and now < self._expiry - 60:  # refresh at 60s left
            return self._token
        with self._lock:
            # double-check after acquiring lock
            if self._token and time.time() < self._expiry - 60:
                return self._token
            self._token, self._expiry = exchange_oidc_for_redwood_token(...)
            return self._token
```

maya: nice. any Node/Go quirks we should call out?

lee: node: avoid storing tokens in process memory if customers run multiple worker processes and expect shared quota. Go: use context for cancellation in streams and ensure token refresh doesn't leak goroutines.

sam: also: for clients that support both org-level and project-level calls, we add an explicit "scope" param on the client and require it at init time if the SA can access multiple projects. prevents accidental cross-project calls.

maya: does the backend require a specific claim name? or multiple accepted patterns?

jared: backend accepts either 'redwood_project' claim, or a scopes array entry like 'redwood:project:proj_123'. we prefer the scope-style for RBAC checks but support both for backwards compat.

maya: perfect. i'll prototype in the python SDK and ping for review. thanks! :thumbsup:

devex-bot: FYI — there's an internal doc draft at https://wiki.internal/redwood/devex/oidc-project-scoping (permissions required).

maya: saw that, will reference it. tagging @lee for follow-up on token provider interface when i open the PR.

lee: happy to review. short follow-up: add tests that simulate mid-stream expiry and assert reconnect behaviour.
